title: Restore a trashed Gmail message with AI
h1: bring a gmail message out of trash
description: Recover a Gmail message from trash by asking a bot to find and restore the exact email. Learn which reference it needs and what recovery cannot promise.
keyword: gmail restore trashed email with ai
answer: if an email is still in gmail trash, a bot can remove it from trash for you. it searches trash for the email you describe, so give it the sender and a rough date. restoring changes the mailbox and needs write access; tell the bot to show you the match before restoring when several emails look alike.
og_line: recover the email you meant to keep.
what:
untrash message removes the trash state from a previously trashed email. it does not recreate an email that is no longer available, and the action does not let you pick a destination folder. it takes the email out of trash; it can't choose which folder it goes to.

the bot searches your trash first and restores the exact email you pick. give it the account, sender and a date or subject so recovery starts from a specific match.
uses: recover the travel confirmation you discarded before checking the ticket number
undo a mistaken cleanup of a customer approval email
restore an old warranty message when the repair shop asks for proof of purchase

routine.message: every evening at 6, check my gmail trash for anything from my accountant, claire@ledgerly.example, that went to trash today. show me the subject and date and ask before restoring. restore only what i choose. never empty trash or restore other mail.
routine.needs: gmail connected, with read and write access to restore messages
routine.output:
ledgerly: 1 email in trash today
subject: your q3 return is ready to sign
restore it? nothing changed yet.

steps: label the intended gmail account in **Connected apps** so recovery does not search a different mailbox.
allow **read and write** for restoration, or keep **read only** if you only want a list of matches.
try recovering a single known email and check in gmail that it is no longer in trash.
check the schedule on the routine card and choose **Pause** when the recovery watch is no longer useful.
watch: a message that has already been permanently removed is outside what untrash can restore.
if you have more than one gmail connected, say which account to look in.
mailbox restores have no automatic sending checkpoint, so the example asks you to choose each message.

faq.q: does restore always put the message in my inbox?
faq.a: this action removes a message from trash. it has no destination input, so do not use it as a promise to place mail in the inbox.

faq.q: can it recover every message from a conversation at once?
faq.a: the input is one message id. ask the bot to identify the individual messages you want recovered and confirm each selection.
